notes: Steven Piano now keeps itself up to date: a new version shows on the Piano tab, and on the school tablet it installs without a tap. Share diagnostics sends the app's logs when something goes wrong.

Channels play your library without end: Calm, Epic, Baroque, Romantic, Impressionist, Nocturnes, Études and Everything, each at its own volume. Popular, Recognisable and Epic on piano fill themselves from your pieces. Left alone for a minute, the tablet becomes a display for passers-by. Every piece starts after a short pause, the score lights the notes it plays in yellow, a mini player (a now-playing panel on tablets) keeps the piece in sight, the controls float on frosted glass, the Piano tab's settings are grouped into pages, and Appearance can follow the system or stay light or dark.

Web control: open the panel in any browser on your Tailscale network to see what is playing, play and queue pieces, browse the library, start channels, adjust the piano, and add pieces by dropping MIDI or zip files onto the page. Guests can request a piece by scanning the printable poster, one request every five minutes, with an approve-first switch. Turn it on under Piano › Remote control and set a six-digit PIN. Also: hardening from the security audit of the panel, a larger title on the standby screen, and small fixes.

Firmware updates from the app: Piano › Firmware and status shows the piano's firmware version, checks for a signed release, and sends it over Bluetooth — the piano goes quiet, receives the image, verifies the signature, restarts, and rolls back by itself if the new firmware fails to start. Needs firmware 2.0.0 on the piano first (one USB flash).
